Chapter 5: Embracing a Global Mission and Caring for the Poor.
Think about this for a moment—the world is so much bigger than our own neighborhoods. For most of us, it’s really easy to forget about the struggles happening miles, or even continents, away. Things like poverty, hunger, disease, and injustice can feel so far removed from our daily routines, almost like they belong in another world.
But if you look at what Jesus taught, there’s no mistaking it—caring for people who are hurting and reaching out to those in need is right at the heart of real faith.
Imagine a group of students spending their summer break volunteering in a place that’s nothing like home. Suddenly, they’re face-to-face with children who don’t have enough to eat, families living in makeshift shelters, and whole communities without clean water. At first, it’s overwhelming. Honestly, who wouldn’t want to just turn away, go back to what’s comfortable, and forget? But then something shifts. Those faces and stories linger, and they start to wonder—what can I do to actually help?
Here’s something most people forget: our world is deeply connected. The choices we make in one corner of the world can create ripples that are felt thousands of miles away. Sometimes, the comforts we enjoy are possible because of systems that leave others in need.
When we talk about a global mission, it’s not just about writing a check or going on a one-time trip. It’s about seeing every single person as valuable, and being willing to act for their good.
The early followers of Jesus really got this. They traveled far from home, cared for the sick, and shared freely with anyone in need. Their faith didn’t stop at the edge of their own communities—it reached across cultures, languages, and borders. They knew they were part of a much bigger story, one that included people from every background and every place.
Let me share a story that really brings this home. There was a retired couple who decided to spend their later years serving in a country they’d never even visited before. They left behind the comfort and familiarity of home, learned a brand-new language, and built friendships with people who’d never heard the message of Jesus. It wasn’t easy. There were tough days and moments of doubt. But over time, they witnessed real change—not just in the lives of those they served, but in their own hearts as well.
Here’s the thing—caring for the poor and embracing a global mission isn’t just for a chosen few. It’s a calling for anyone who wants to follow Jesus with their whole life. It means stepping out of what’s comfortable, really seeing the needs of others, and acting with compassion and generosity. It’s about realizing that faith isn’t just something private—it’s meant to make a difference in the world.
So, let me ask you—where do you see an opportunity to serve, to give, to make a real impact? This journey isn’t always easy, but if you’re willing to take the first step, you’ll discover a faith that’s bold, outward-looking, and truly transformative.
